lead.headline: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home in criminal probe
lead.dek: Omar calls the search political intimidation; Trump says he had "nothing to do with it"
body: Homeland Security Investigations agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington-area home Monday under a court-authorized warrant, the Justice Department said, in what a person familiar with the case told NBC News is a yearslong criminal investigation involving immigration and fraud.

The department's statement did not name the Minnesota Democrat or say what the investigation concerns, and no charges have been filed. Omar wrote on X that the search was "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement" and said, "I will not be silenced." Trump told reporters he had "nothing to do with it" and that investigators were "looking at her very carefully."

The search came 22 days before the midterm elections, in which Omar is running for re-election. House Democratic leaders Hakeem Jeffries, Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar called it "deeply disturbing." Vice President JD Vance has accused Omar of immigration fraud, which she denies, and Trump raised her Somali origin again at a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, Monday night.

briefs.headline: Trump rallies in Youngstown for Husted, attacks Omar and Minnesota
briefs.summary: Trump told an Ohio crowd Monday night to back Sen. Jon Husted over Sherrod Brown and Vivek Ramaswamy for governor to "stop Ohio from being plundered, ransacked and destroyed like Minnesota." The crowd chanted "deport."

briefs.headline: 911 calls show half-hour delay after Christa Pike's failed execution
briefs.summary: Recordings reviewed by AP show the first call from Tennessee's execution chamber at 8:40 p.m. Sept. 30; dispatchers were told it was false and prison officials confirmed it at 9:11 p.m.

briefs.headline: Americans Hall and Woodford win Nobel economics prize
briefs.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences on Monday cited their models for stabilizing economies against shocks, which it said underpin those now used by central banks. They share $1.2 million.

briefs.headline: Erie coroner names gunman and six of the eight victims
briefs.summary: Coroner Lyell Cook said Monday that Matthew Stone Sr., 45, killed his wife, pregnant daughter, two sons, two grandchildren and two women outside the house Friday before killing himself. Police have given no motive.

briefs.headline: Simon weakens offshore as Mexico storms kill 5
briefs.summary: Hurricane Simon's eye stayed about 100 miles off Cabo Corrientes early Tuesday with 90 mph winds and no landfall. Four died in Baja California floods from Rachel's remnants and a man in Guerrero.

briefs.headline: Ethiopian forces enter Tigray town of Adwa, residents say
briefs.summary: Federal troops entered Adwa, 24 miles from the Eritrean border, on Sunday a day after TPLF fighters withdrew, residents told AFP. Ethiopia took Mekelle last week.

briefs.headline: Nepal flood strands more than 100 foreign trekkers
briefs.summary: A landslide-triggered flash flood on the Budhi Gandaki swept away part of the Manaslu trail and 200 homes in Gorkha. Authorities rescued 321 people Monday; five villagers are missing.

briefs.headline: Pope Leo XIV enters Gemelli hospital for lung surgery
briefs.summary: The 71-year-old pope was admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital Tuesday to have a small lung nodule, which he said was found at an early stage, removed. It is his first hospitalization since his election in May 2025.

briefs.headline: State seeks outside operators for Bateman, Sharpe hospitals
briefs.summary: The Department of Health Facilities issued a request for proposals Monday for private management of its two psychiatric hospitals in Huntington and Weston. Both stay state-owned; Sharpe's costs top $128 million a year.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers ask Flock to testify in person, under oath
briefs.summary: Four House delegates sent Flock Safety a seventh letter with 19 questions and asked for a public hearing at the Nov. 9 interims. Flock said it has given nearly two hours of testimony and 18 pages of answers.

briefs.headline: Appeals court upholds $30M judgment against Justice
briefs.summary: The Sixth Circuit on Friday affirmed that Sen. Jim Justice personally owes Lexon Insurance nearly $30 million on coal-company bond guarantees he signed as governor, rejecting his bid to cap liability at $3.5 million.

briefs.headline: Voter registration closes today for Nov. 3 election
briefs.summary: Tuesday is the deadline to register or update a registration for the general election; early voting opens Oct. 21. Clerks said polls are staffed but still want alternate poll workers.

regional.item: Marshall's fall enrollment is 13,094, up 1.5% and a fourth straight rise, the university told its board, the Herald-Dispatch said Monday.
Kanawha schools told the board Monday every third-grade family got a letter on the new retention law, which tests in April.
The U.S. 33 Ritchie Bridge at Ravenswood closes nightly 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. through October for deck work, with detours posted.
AWAY holds a free noon candlelight vigil for domestic violence victims Thursday at Summersville City Hall, with lunch served.

away.item: State preservation officials said last week a full Bennington Monument restoration could reach $40 million; the elevator stays closed.

hotspots.item: A second air test at Webster County High School found no mold or bacteria, the superintendent told the school board Sept. 28, the Echo reported Oct. 6.
North Topsail Beach moved its Howl-O-Ween pet parade to Town Hall because of flood-mitigation work at Richard C. Peters Park, the town said Monday.

briefs.headline: UNBC sets first UNBC Week for Oct. 19-25
briefs.summary: Interim president Bill Owen said the week opens campus to the public, with Timberwolves Legacy Night Oct. 21, Discovery Day Oct. 23 and free home games.

briefs.headline: Williams Lake mayor faces former mayor Cobb Oct. 17
briefs.summary: Incumbent Surinderpal Rathor, elected in 2022 after 21 years on council, is challenged by Walt Cobb, mayor from 1990-96 and 2014-22, in the city of 11,100.

briefs.headline: Eby warns of privatized care; Conservatives cry fearmongering
briefs.summary: The NDP leader said Monday a Conservative government would copy Alberta's public-private doctor model. The party said it will keep B.C. care universal and publicly funded.

briefs.headline: Eby urges Albertans to vote for unity in Thanksgiving message
briefs.summary: The B.C. NDP leader said Sunday the two provinces are "stronger together" and he hopes Alberta rejects a second, binding referendum on leaving in the Oct. 19 vote.

briefs.headline: CBSA seeks to deport Liberal donor over China war-crime claims
briefs.summary: The agency alleges Rong Xiang Yuan, 63, founder of a Canada-China friendship group, committed crimes against humanity as a PLA platoon leader in the 1980s. He denies it; no IRB hearing date is set.

briefs.headline: Alberta advance polls open with 650,000 special ballots requested
briefs.summary: Elections Alberta reported the requests, against 59,000 in 2023, as five days of advance voting began Tuesday for the Oct. 19 vote. Carney's office said he will visit Alberta in the coming days.

briefs.headline: Snakebite study puts global deaths at up to 513,000 a year
briefs.summary: A PLOS Medicine review of data from 79 countries estimates 2.1 million to 7 million envenomings a year and 274,000 to 513,000 deaths, 45% of them in sub-Saharan Africa.

briefs.headline: Perseverance passes Opportunity for off-world driving record
briefs.summary: NASA's rover logged 28.10 miles on Sunday, its 2,006th sol, topping Opportunity's 28.06 miles; JPL said the original mission called for no more than 12.4 miles.

briefs.headline: Satellite survey finds 465 cities sinking, Medan fastest
briefs.summary: A Nature Cities study of 2014-2023 radar data in 107 countries put Medan's median subsidence at 33 mm a year; parts of Mexico City dropped about 217 mm a year.

briefs.headline: NOAA keeps G1 storm forecast for Tuesday after quiet Monday
briefs.summary: SWPC's 8:30 p.m. ET forecast said minor storm conditions are likely Tuesday from a coronal hole stream; Monday's peak Kp was 3, below storm level, and overnight readings reached 3.33.

briefs.headline: Home Office asylum AI summaries failed 22% of expert checks
briefs.summary: Open Rights Group said 45 of 203 GPT-4o interview summaries failed review after an April rollout, up from 9% in the pilot, and called for both Home Office tools to be suspended.

briefs.headline: White House restores UK AI Security Institute's model access
briefs.summary: The Daily Telegraph reported the administration lifted a September order telling Anthropic, Google DeepMind and OpenAI to stop sharing pre-release models with the institute.

briefs.headline: Meta's Muse Wonder scores 56 on independent intelligence index
briefs.summary: Artificial Analysis put Muse Wonder Full at 56, up from Muse Spark's 48, with a 23% hallucination rate; Meta priced the API model at $4 per million input tokens.

kicker: Summers-New River carries no regional line today; Monday's rain on the Williams River is read in Sports & Sportsman.
